review_candidates.description: The Program Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for HIAS programs in Panama, ensuring that interventions are responsive to the priorities, capacities, protection risks and evolving needs of refugees, asylum seekers, migrants and displaced populations. The position leads the planning, implementation, monitoring and continuous adaptation of community-based programming where HIAS Panama operates. Panama is both a transit and host country for refugees, displaced people, and migrants in Latin America. While migration policies have changed across the Americas, hundreds of thousands of displaced people still need humanitarian assistance as they move across the country, headed north and south, particularly in the border areas of Darien and Chiriquí, but with many of them staying in Panama City. In 2025, Panama hosted more than 155,000 displaced people, including over 5,000 refugees and 36,500 asylum seekers. More than half of those in need of protection come from Venezuela, while thousands of others originate from countries across Central America. While migratory flows in transit through Panama have decreased over the last two years, people continue to cross through the Darien jungle via new and invisible routes, and there is a constant transit of people migrating south, seeking to return to Colombia and/or Venezuela. In the face of decreasing humanitarian aid funds worldwide, many organizations have ceased or scaled back operations in Panama, leaving HIAS as one of the few organizations currently providing assistance and protection services to these populations. The position promotes an integrated approach encompassing legal protection, community-based protection, including MHPSS and GBV prevention and response, economic empowerment and other urgent protection and assistance needs consistent with HIAS' programming. Essential Functions Business Development and Program Design: Develop proposals for fundraising opportunities from existing and new donors. Ensure programming recognizes the different needs of people in transit, in reverse movement, seeking asylum, or pursuing longer-term integration in Panama. Establish mechanisms that enable communities to participate meaningfully in program design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Translate assessment findings, community feedback and program data into practical program priorities, implementation plans and resource decisions. Identify geographic and service gaps and recommend appropriate adjustments or expansion of programming. Participate in the development of the strategic and operational plan for programs at the national level. Program Management And Implementation Lead the implementation of programs according to approved proposals, workplans, budgets, donor requirements and HIAS technical standards. Establish implementation plans with clear milestones, responsibilities, indicators and community-level outcomes. Work collaboratively with government and nongovernmental institutions to strengthen the response to the needs of the refugee, asylum-seeking, and migrant populations in the country. Advise Country Management on programmatic priorities, risks, and resource requirements, including human, financial, technical, and logistical needs necessary for effective program delivery. Manage the internal implementation of prevention protocols in response to survivors of gender-based violence. Analyze and consolidate information to generate statistical and narrative reports in accordance with the requirements of the Organization, the Headquarters, or donors. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning Regularly monitor program implementation and introduce timely corrective actions when services are not adequately addressing identified needs. Manage, with the Monitoring and Evaluation department, the process of preparing both internal and external management reports. Identify and implement improvements or adjustments to program procedures and ways to strengthen the teams’ technical knowledge, in accordance with the demands and requirements of the local context. Establish and oversee procedures for recording information and maintaining records at the program level to ensure their quality and confidentiality. Grants, Budgets & Donor Compliance Provide oversight and management for program development, staffing, and budgeting, in collaboration with Financial Management and Country Management. Participate in budget-versus-actual reviews and ensure programmatic explanations and corrective actions are provided for significant variances. Ensure accurate, evidence-based and timely donor reporting. Work closely with Finance, Grants and technical teams to ensure donor and organizational compliance. Identify programmatic and operational risks and maintain appropriate mitigation measures. Team Leadership & Capacity Building Provide clear programmatic leadership and technical direction to program teams. Establish clear roles, performance expectations and accountability for program results. Identify staff capacity-development needs and coordinate appropriate coaching, training and technical assistance. Foster collaboration between field teams and support areas: Finance, Human Resources, Safety & Security and others. Promote a management culture grounded in HIAS values. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications & Requirements Professional degree in a social sciences field; a master’s degree or specialization in social project management is preferred. 10+ years experience in project management at international NGO, and/or working with vulnerable populations in situations of forced displacement.5+ years of management experience Advanced English proficiency, with the ability to conduct negotiations and deliver effective presentations in the language. Proficiency with Office 365 applications for collaborative work. Experience with databases. Budget management. Ability to work in a multicultural team. Ability to travel frequently within Panama and internationally as required. Job may require traveling and working in insecure operating environments. Selection Process We are committed to a fair and respectful hiring process, and we make every effort to respond to each of our applicants. We prioritize communication and transparency with all our candidates, including those who are not selected to move forward in the process. Here is a brief description of the current process: Step 1: Submit your application through our platform Step 2: Initial contact with Human Resources via phone call or email Step 3: In-depth interview with Human Resources Step 4: Panel interview with your direct supervisor and the technical team Step 5: Reference checks and background screening Step 6: Offer letter Step 7: Begin your professional journey at HIAS Note: Some of our processes may vary, and not all candidates advance to the next stages. About Us For over a century, the Jewish community of HIAS (Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society) has been based in New York City, America’s gateway for immigrants. In helping Jewish people escape persecution and poverty in Eastern Europe, our founders were guided by the traditions, texts, and history of the Jewish community—a history of resilience, migration, and displacement. HIAS has helped generations of Jews who have faced violence simply for being who they are, and HIAS remains committed to helping Jewish refugees anywhere in the world. review_candidates.title: Director of Operations, Slate Development
review_candidates.description: Scopely is looking for a Director, Slate Operations to join our Slate Development Group team in the UK remotely or in Barcelona, on a flexible hybrid model. At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily. Slate Operations keeps Scopely's game development slate moving. We oversee execution and cross-functional alignment across the games in development — connecting game teams and central teams so decisions get made once and stick, running the cadence that keeps everyone aligned, and clearing the path so teams can build. What You'll Do We're looking for a Director, Slate Operations to own this end to end. There are two sides to it: keeping the Group running as an organization — its cadence, process, and the day-to-day support the Game Board, Head of Slate Development and leadership team rely on — and running program management for the Game Development Framework (GDF) so games move cleanly from concept to launch. You'll sit inside the Slate Development Group but work with every part of Scopely: game teams, divisional leadership, finance, strategy, and corporate development. Be the operational point of contact for specific in-development games — running the GDF cadence and connecting game and central teams so decisions get made once and aren't re-litigated. The main goal is to be the end to end steward for game teams in the game development framework. Deliver operational excellence within our internal team, shaping our service model, priorities, and ways of working. Evolve our capabilities as needs change. Drive the cross-slate operating model so independent game teams reuse what already works instead of rebuilding it. Bring structure to consequential decisions — organize the inputs, assumptions, and trade-offs early so the owners and the room can reach real alignment before committing. Own a capstone project — one meaty area you drive end to end, for example: evolving the GDF, owning launch readiness, or operationalizing central partnerships, depending on where the need is. Keep investment decisions well-informed — track progress across games at different stages, and surface Greenlight Case, budget, staffing, and dependency status so leadership can challenge and decide. Unblock teams through the development cycle, especially at launch readiness, by clearing operational issues with central partners (legal, IT, procurement, finance, logistics) so teams stay focused on the game. Partner with marketing, strategy, and divisional leadership so launches go out clean. Give teams operational support — production perspective, process, facilitation, and help navigating the GDF. Operationalize playtests and validation — help build and run research, playtest, and validation plans, and package the findings so vertical owners and leaders can form the recommendation. Utilize the latest AI technologies to keep information flowing — the dashboards, status, and key dates people need to see, without the overhead. What We’re Looking For Bachelor's degree, MBA a plus — or the equivalent in experience. 10+ years in program/project management across tech and direct-to-consumer businesses, at least 5 of them in games, working within or alongside a development team. You know how games get made and sold — development, publishing, platforms, business models. You don't need to have shipped one yourself, but you get what game teams are up against. You've supported senior execs in a fast-moving environment and you like the pace — taking initiative, juggling priorities, switching gears without losing the thread. You can run a lot of projects at once, ideally a mix of R&D and live. You're comfortable in ambiguity and good at creating clarity for other people. You make sound calls in the company's interest and know when to escalate. You can hold your own with P&Ls and free-to-play KPIs. You spot the process that's slowing people down and fix it — and you'll push back and start the right debate when it matters. You build trust with all kinds of people at every level and don't flinch at the hard conversations — with the presence to grow into a partner to senior game leaders over time. You write clearly and fast, and you can build a strong deck with cross-functional input. Detail and organization come naturally to you. Low ego, business outcomes first, open to feedback — and genuinely curious about every part of the business. You play games and care about the industry. About Scopely Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play. Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come. Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play. Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: https://www.scopely.com/.
